page: Amazon Web Services m8a.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose EC2 instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs (1 thread per core) clocking at up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory rated at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per core). It does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, and it provisions a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread execution efficiency. The m8a.2xlarge places in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core performance (3771.59), Geekbench single-core score (2817.0), single-threaded gzip compression (41.48 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (18.15 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks align with mid-range 8-vCPU expectations, registering within the middle 50% for Geekbench multi-core (14151.0), stress-ng multi-core (30095.61), and PassMark CPU score (25641.67). Memory throughput yields 54.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 34.26 GB/sec for writes. Small-model LLM inference benchmarks reflect notable performance, achieving 415.91 tokens/sec for 135M model text generation, while medium 7B model generation settles into the middle tier at 12.63 tokens/sec.

The qualitative trade-off of the m8a.2xlarge centers on dedicated compute power versus local I/O dependencies. With 8 full physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, workloads benefit from predictable execution without thread contention. However, because local ephemeral storage is absent, all persistent and scratch storage depends entirely on network-attached volumes, bounded by the instance baseline network bandwidth. The instance is optimal for balanced workloads with high per-thread demands, such as application backends, mid-sized database management systems, static web serving, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight CPU-based inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.2xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with an 8-core AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture with 1 thread per physical core. It provides 32.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The instance features no local storage and no GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark results reflect leading single-thread performance, ranking in the top 10% for single-core Geekbench and stress-ng tests, as well as text processing and compression tasks. Multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and database metrics perform consistently within average industry ranges. With strong dedicated single-core throughput, the m8a.2xlarge is well tailored for enterprise web serving, backend services, CI/CD builds, and mid-tier transactional databases.
